$comment: Declared versions NOT published from this repository, each with the reason.
State is computed from this repository's git tags. a1 and a2 were published
from dotmac_starter_mt and their tags stay there permanently.
EMPTY, and that is the correct state: every declared version is published.
0.1.0a3 is published and permanently unpinnable; 0.1.0a4 is published,
independently verified, and refused for adoption on Michael's ruling of
2026-08-30; 0.1.0a5 is published and verified on all seven properties.
None of the three is an unpublished declaration, so none belongs here —
`docs/published-versions.json` is where all three live, and a4's superseding
disposition is appended to its original PASS record there rather than
replacing it.
The a4 row that used to sit here said `never-published` and outlived its own
publication by six hours. That is the stale absolution the two-directional
ratchet in test_ported_gate_declared_publication.py exists to catch, and it
did not catch it: CI checked out without tags, so the gate could not see the
tag that contradicted this file. Both halves are fixed together — the row is
gone and the checkout now fetches tags.
The 0.1.0a5 row that sat here between the declaration and the publication is
gone in the change that records the coordinates, which is the discipline the
a4 row failed. A row here and a row in docs/published-versions.json are
never both true at once, and a test states that over the two FILES so it
holds even in a tagless checkout.
